title.narrative: Storm Anna & Cyclone Batsirai 2022 - Southern Africa

description.narrative: Tropical Storm Ana made landfall in Madagascar on January 22nd 2022 - it then crossed the Mozambique Channel making landfall in Nampula Province, Mozambique on the 24th Jan, it continued westwards affecting the northern part of Zambezia province, through Central and Southern Malawi then and the southern part of Mozambique's Tete province. Mozambique - 126,963 people affected (will increase), 7.5 million IFRC wide funding (some from Eloise) required to support 50,000 people / 10,000 HH. Support - integrated assistance, health and care including WASH and Protection and Prevention Malawi - 536,352 people affected, 6.5 million IFRC wide funding required to support 160,000 people/ 32,000HH, DREF 750,000. Support - integrated assistance, health and care including WASH and Protection and Prevention. Cyclone Batsirai made landfall in Madagascar on Saturday 5th February, going South along the country before entering the Mozambique channel and continuing South into the ocean. Madagascar - 736,600 people affected 3 million Preliminary Emergency Appeal to assist 50,000 people (10,000 HH) DREF 750,000. Support - integrated assistance, health and care including WASH and Protection and Prevention.

This is the transfer of FCDO funds to IFRC emergency appeal in response to cyclone Batsirai in Madagascar. Due to delays from IFRC side we have not received the pledge number yet. The transfer should thus clearly mention that those funds are earmarked to Cyclone Batsirai Emergency appeal (Madagascar) as per GAD signed between both parties. GBP 490,000 to be transferred to IFRC. Remaining GBP 10,000 (i.e., 2% of the total contribution) is retained by BRC to cover its admin costs.

This is the transfer of Scottish Government funds to IFRC emergency appeal in response to Storm Ana in Malawi. Due to delays from IFRC side we have not received the pledge number yet. The transfer should thus clearly mention that those funds are earmarked to Storm Ana Emergency Appeal (Malawi) as per GAD. IFRC will share the pledge number as soon as available so we can update the system.
